title: Asset ownership proof an audit issue
full_text:
The ATO has revealed the lack of appropriate evidence regarding the existence and ownership of fund assets is a common flaw in the files of SMSF auditors.
“That’s generally for listed investments and crypto-assets. We often find a holding statement on the audit file, but no other evidence [and] the holding statement alone isn’t sufficient to support ownership and existence due to the possibility that holding statement of course could be manipulated,” ATO SMSF branch director Kellie Grant told attendees of the recent SMSF Association Audit Day 2026.
“[So we] expect the auditor has checked that holding statement against another independent sources.”
As an extension of this issue, Grant pointed out the lack of Type 2 reports was also of concern for the regulator.
“We also very rarely see Type 2 reports to support the controls in place for service organisations that invest on behalf of the fund or any substantive testing carried out to support the auditor’s opinion on the fund’s compliance,” she revealed.
Even though she identified this is an issue, she confirmed the ATO does apply a common-sense approach to it.
“While we understand auditors can’t always get those Type 2 GS (Guidance Statement) 007 reports, we would at least expect to see a Part A of the audit report being qualified in that sort of instance if they can’t get any other evidence to support the controls,” she said.
According to Grant, overreliance on data feeds is another area auditors must address in their procedures.
“We’ve found that many auditors are relying on data feeds without obtaining a Type 2 report or carrying out any testing on the data feed to support its reliability,” she explained.
“So for instance, if the data feed is for a fund’s bank account, we would expect the audit file to include the opening bank account statement and the closing statement and that would hopefully then provide the auditor with some confidence that the data feed is correct.”
She referred practitioners to GS 009 for guidance on the use of data feeds.
